title: A day at work (Mein Arbeitstag)
summary: Talk about your work day: the people (Chef, Kunde, Team), the tasks (E-Mails, telefonieren, drucken), and when things start and end.
goals: Name people and things at work: Chef, Kunde, Team, Büro
Say what you do at work: E-Mails schreiben, telefonieren, drucken
Say when you start and whether you're finished

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A1, chapter 9: Working life (Ich bin Lehrerin, Mein Beruf)

items.de: Um zehn hat er einen Termin.
items.en: At ten he has an appointment.
At twelve he takes a break.

items.de: Am Nachmittag hat er viele Aufgaben.
items.en: In the afternoon he has lots of tasks.

items.de: Um fünf ist er fertig und hat Feierabend.
items.en: At five he's done and finishes work.

sections.title: What you do at work
sections.text:
- [[E-Mails schreiben]], [[eine E-Mail schicken]]
- [[telefonieren]] = to be on the phone: [[Der Chef telefoniert.]]
- [[drucken]] = to print
- [[beginnen]] = to begin: [[Der Kurs beginnt um neun.]] (the same as [[anfangen]] from Unit 3, but not separable)
- [[Pause machen]], [[Feierabend haben]] (Unit 3)

With the modal verbs from Unit 3: [[Ich muss das noch drucken.]] [[Kannst du die E-Mail schicken?]]

[[fertig]] = done, finished: [[Bist du fertig?]] - [[Ja!]] / [[Noch nicht.]] And [[wichtig]] = important: [[Das ist wichtig.]]

sections.title: -in for women
sections.text: As with [[Lehrer]] and [[Lehrerin]] in Unit 1: [[der Chef]], [[die Chefin]]; [[der Kunde]], [[die Kundin]]; [[der Kollege]], [[die Kollegin]].

sections.title: du or Sie at work?
sections.text: In many German offices, especially in tech, colleagues say [[du]] from the first day. With the boss and with customers, start with [[Sie]]. Usually the boss or the older person offers [[du]]: [[Wir können gern du sagen.]]

items.en: The boss is on the phone.
I still have to print that.

items.question: Which word means 'customer'?
items.explanation: der Kunde, die Kundin = customer. der Chef = boss, der Kollege = colleague.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap with beginnen: Work starts at nine.
items.explanation: die Arbeit beginnt: the time first, then the verb.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: I still have to print that.
items.explanation: muss in second place, drucken at the end.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: Are you done?

items.prompt: In the afternoon I write emails.
items.explanation: Whatever comes first, the verb is second.
